packs.title: Food, Cooking & Everyday Nutrition
packs.subject: Food & Nutrition
packs.description: 20 questions on food safety, cooking skills, balanced meals and nutrition basics.

questions.question: Why should hands be washed before preparing food?
options: To reduce the spread of microbes to food
To increase the water content of fruit
questions.explanation: Clean hands lower the chance of transferring harmful microbes.

questions.question: What is a balanced meal?
options: A plate containing one food only
A meal including varied food groups in suitable proportions
questions.explanation: Variety helps provide different nutrients.

questions.question: Which nutrient is an important source of energy?
questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are one source of energy for the body.

questions.question: What is protein useful for?
options: Growth and repair of body tissues
questions.explanation: Protein supplies amino acids used to build and repair tissues.

questions.question: What do dietary fibres help support?
questions.explanation: Fibre supports digestive health.

questions.question: Why is clean drinking water important?
options: It has no role in digestion
It helps the body stay hydrated
questions.explanation: Water is essential for many normal body processes.

questions.question: Which method best lowers the risk of cross-contamination?
options: Touch cooked food after handling raw meat without washing
Store raw chicken above fresh salad
Use separate tools or clean them between raw meat and ready-to-eat food
Use one dirty board for all ingredients
questions.explanation: Separation and cleaning reduce transfer of harmful microorganisms.

questions.question: Why should raw poultry be cooked thoroughly?
options: To make it weigh exactly twice as much
questions.explanation: Adequate cooking destroys many dangerous microorganisms.

questions.question: Why should foods be stored at appropriate temperatures?
options: To slow harmful microbial growth and spoilage
To change every food into ice
To remove the need to wash produce
questions.explanation: Temperature control is a key part of food safety.

questions.question: What does a food ingredient list show?
options: Ingredients used to make a packaged product
questions.explanation: Ingredient lists help consumers understand what is in a product.

questions.question: Which is a healthy approach to eating?
options: Eat the same snack for every meal
Choose varied foods and listen to hunger and fullness cues
Skip all meals to study longer
questions.explanation: Balanced eating and routine habits support health.

questions.question: Why can home cooking be a useful skill?
options: It helps people plan ingredients, hygiene and portion choices
It guarantees all meals are perfect
questions.explanation: Cooking skills support informed food preparation.

questions.question: What are legumes?
options: Plants such as beans, peas and lentils
questions.explanation: Legumes are edible seeds from plants in the legume family.

questions.question: Which food group commonly provides calcium?
questions.explanation: Dairy and some fortified alternatives can contribute calcium.

questions.question: What is a recipe's ingredient quantity for?
options: Measuring what is needed to prepare a dish
questions.explanation: Correct quantities improve consistency and reduce waste.

questions.question: A recipe serves four people. For eight people, what should you usually do to ingredient amounts?
questions.explanation: Doubling servings generally doubles ingredient quantities.

questions.question: Why should vegetables be washed before eating?
options: To remove some dirt and surface contamination
To eliminate the need for safe storage
To add protein to every vegetable
questions.explanation: Washing can remove soil and some contaminants.

questions.question: What is food waste?
options: Food intended for consumption that is discarded
questions.explanation: Wasted food uses resources without being eaten.

questions.question: Which method helps reduce food waste at home?
options: Plan portions and safely use leftovers
Buy more than you can store
questions.explanation: Planning and proper storage reduce unnecessary waste.

questions.question: Why is the nutrition information panel useful?
options: It tells you who bought the food
It helps compare energy and nutrient amounts across foods
It proves every product is healthy
questions.explanation: Nutrition panels provide standardised information for comparison.

packs.title: Weather Watchers & Climate Patterns
packs.subject: Weather
packs.description: 20 questions on clouds, rainfall, forecasts and safe weather awareness.

questions.question: What instrument measures rainfall amount?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects rainfall to measure its depth.

questions.question: What is air pressure?
options: The force of air acting over an area
questions.explanation: Air has mass and exerts pressure.

questions.question: What does an anemometer measure?
questions.explanation: Anemometers are used to measure wind speed.

questions.question: How do many clouds form?
options: Water vapour cools and condenses into droplets or ice crystals
questions.explanation: Condensation produces droplets and crystals suspended in air.

questions.question: What is humidity?
options: The number of birds in a tree
The amount of water vapour in the air
questions.explanation: Humidity describes atmospheric water vapour.

questions.question: What is the main difference between weather and climate?
options: Weather is short-term conditions; climate is long-term patterns
Weather lasts centuries; climate lasts one minute
questions.explanation: Climate is described using longer-term statistics of weather.

questions.question: What causes a rainbow?
options: Sunlight refracting, reflecting and dispersing in water droplets
questions.explanation: Light interacts with droplets to create a spectrum.

questions.question: What is a thunderstorm?
options: A storm with lightning and thunder
questions.explanation: Electrical activity in storm clouds causes lightning.

questions.question: During nearby lightning, what is the safest general place to be?
questions.explanation: Indoor shelter is safer during lightning.

questions.question: Why can steep slopes be dangerous after heavy rain?
options: Water may destabilise soil and contribute to landslides
questions.explanation: Saturated ground can increase slope failure risk.

questions.question: What does a weather forecast estimate?
options: Which song will be popular tomorrow
Likely atmospheric conditions over a period
questions.explanation: Forecasts use observations and models to estimate future conditions.

questions.question: Which measurement describes temperature?
questions.explanation: Temperature is commonly measured in Celsius.

questions.question: What is the monsoon?
options: A seasonal pattern of winds associated with rainfall changes
questions.explanation: Monsoon circulations influence seasonal rainfall in many regions.

questions.question: Why do meteorologists use weather satellites?
options: To observe cloud patterns and atmospheric features
questions.explanation: Satellite data supplements surface observations.

questions.question: Why are storm drains important in cities?
options: They carry away excess surface water when functioning properly
They increase every flood risk automatically
questions.explanation: Drainage systems manage runoff, within design limits.

questions.question: What is evaporation in the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Evaporation moves water from surfaces into the air.

questions.question: What is a drought?
options: A period of excess flooding everywhere
A prolonged period of unusually low water availability
questions.explanation: Drought reflects extended water shortages.

questions.question: Why are heat warnings useful?
options: They help people plan hydration, shade and reduced heat exposure
questions.explanation: Heat advisories communicate elevated heat risk.

questions.question: What makes a sea breeze more likely during daytime near the coast?
options: Land heating more quickly than nearby sea water
questions.explanation: Uneven heating can create local air circulation.

questions.question: Why should a school have a weather emergency plan?
options: To guide safe shelter, communications and activities
To ensure there will never be storms
questions.explanation: Prepared procedures help people respond effectively.

packs.title: Wildlife, Habitats & Biodiversity
packs.subject: Animals & Nature
packs.description: 20 questions about animal adaptations, habitats, conservation and ecosystems.

questions.question: What is biodiversity?
options: The variety of living organisms and ecological systems
The number of buildings in a city
questions.explanation: Biodiversity includes species, genetic and ecosystem diversity.

questions.question: What is a habitat?
options: The natural place where an organism lives
Only a type of zoo ticket
questions.explanation: Habitats provide resources and conditions for organisms.

questions.question: Why do birds have different beak shapes?
options: They are adapted for different foods and ways of feeding
All birds eat the same seeds
questions.explanation: Beak form is linked to diet and ecological role.

questions.question: What is camouflage?
options: A type of artificial intelligence model
Features that help an organism blend with surroundings
questions.explanation: Camouflage can make animals harder to detect.

questions.question: What is a nocturnal animal?
options: An animal active mainly at night
questions.explanation: Nocturnal species are primarily active after dark.

questions.question: What is migration in animals?
questions.explanation: Migration can follow seasonal food and breeding opportunities.

questions.question: Which animal is an amphibian?
questions.explanation: Frogs are amphibians with life stages linked to water and land.

questions.question: What is an invertebrate?
questions.explanation: Invertebrates include insects, molluscs and many other groups.

questions.question: Why are wetlands valuable?
options: They provide habitat, filter some pollutants and store water
questions.explanation: Wetlands support biodiversity and water regulation.

questions.question: What can happen if an important pollinator declines?
options: No flowering plant can reproduce at all
Some plants may produce fewer fruits or seeds
questions.explanation: Many plants benefit from animal pollination.

questions.question: What is an endangered species?
options: A species facing a high risk of extinction
A species that is always common
questions.explanation: Endangered classifications reflect elevated extinction risk.

questions.question: What does a conservation programme try to do?
options: Replace every wild animal with a robot
Protect species, habitats or natural resources
questions.explanation: Conservation aims to sustain ecosystems and species.

questions.question: Why should wild animals not be fed unfamiliar human foods?
options: All human food is suitable for wildlife
It may harm their health and natural behaviour
questions.explanation: Feeding wildlife can introduce poor diets and dependence.

questions.question: What is a keystone species?
options: Any tree older than ten years
A species whose influence on its ecosystem is unusually large
Only the largest animal in a zoo
An organism living only in caves
questions.explanation: Some species strongly shape ecosystem interactions.

questions.question: Why are connected wildlife corridors useful?
options: They help animals move between fragmented habitats
questions.explanation: Corridors can maintain movement and genetic exchange.

questions.question: What is a food chain?
options: A metal chain used in farming
A simple sequence showing who eats whom
questions.explanation: Food chains represent the transfer of energy through feeding.

questions.question: What is an invasive species?
options: A species found in its original home
A plant that always produces flowers
A non-native organism that spreads and causes ecological harm
Any animal in a nature reserve
questions.explanation: Some introduced species can damage native ecosystems.

questions.question: Why do some animals have thick fur in cold environments?
options: It can help reduce heat loss
It prevents the need for food
questions.explanation: Insulating fur helps maintain body temperature.

questions.question: What is an example of symbiosis?
options: Two different species living in close ecological association
A thunderstorm moving across a city
questions.explanation: Symbiosis refers to close interactions between distinct species.

questions.question: Which activity helps protect local wildlife?
options: Respect habitats and avoid disturbing nests
questions.explanation: Reducing disturbance protects animals and habitat.

packs.title: Critical Thinking & Smart Decisions
packs.subject: Critical Thinking
packs.description: 20 scenarios about reasoning, evaluating evidence, probability and thoughtful choices.

questions.question: A friend says 'everyone likes this game'. What should you ask?
options: Can the game have more colours?
How loud can the claim be repeated?
questions.explanation: Broad claims need evidence about the relevant group.

questions.question: What is a logical conclusion?
options: A claim that follows from evidence and reasoning
questions.explanation: Sound conclusions are supported by relevant reasons.

questions.question: A study shows two events happen together. What does that prove by itself?
options: They are associated, not necessarily that one causes the other
questions.explanation: Correlation alone does not establish causation.

questions.question: Which is the best question when solving a problem?
options: How can we make the problem sound bigger?
What exactly is the problem we need to solve?
questions.explanation: Clear problem definitions guide solutions.

questions.question: You hear two conflicting claims. What is a good next step?
options: Check evidence and the reliability of each source
questions.explanation: Evidence quality matters more than confidence.

questions.question: Which is an example of a testable prediction?
options: If plants receive less water, their growth may change
This plant is the prettiest ever
The colour green is always best
questions.explanation: A prediction is testable when observations can support or challenge it.

questions.question: What is an assumption?
options: An idea accepted without being directly established in the argument
questions.explanation: Assumptions can influence reasoning and should be examined.

questions.question: Why is it useful to consider an alternative explanation?
options: It removes the need for testing
It can reveal whether the first explanation is sufficient
It guarantees the first idea is wrong
questions.explanation: Competing hypotheses help test reasoning.

questions.question: A claim uses only one success story to promise results for everyone. What is the weakness?
options: One example may not represent a wider group
questions.explanation: Anecdotes do not establish general outcomes.

questions.question: What is a fair comparison in an experiment?
options: Change one main variable while controlling other relevant conditions
questions.explanation: Controlling conditions helps isolate effects.

questions.question: Why use a checklist for a complex task?
options: It guarantees no item will ever change
It helps avoid forgetting important steps
questions.explanation: Checklists support consistency and memory.

questions.question: A shop offers 'buy two, get one free'. What should you check?
options: The number of stars in the logo
Whether you need three items and the total cost
questions.explanation: An offer is useful only if it fits real needs and budget.

questions.question: What is a decision criterion?
options: A standard used to compare possible choices
questions.explanation: Criteria clarify what matters for a choice.

questions.question: Why do scientists report limitations of a study?
options: To explain uncertainty and where results may not apply
questions.explanation: Limitations help readers interpret results appropriately.

questions.question: What is an example of circular reasoning?
options: This claim is true because it is correct
questions.explanation: Circular reasoning assumes what it claims to prove.

questions.question: What is a counterexample?
options: An instance that challenges a general claim
questions.explanation: One valid counterexample can disprove a universal statement.

questions.question: A forecast says a 30% chance of rain. What does it communicate?
options: Rain is possible but not certain in the forecast conditions
Rain will cover exactly 30% of each road
questions.explanation: Probability estimates likelihood, not guaranteed outcomes.

questions.question: Why should a group identify constraints before designing a solution?
options: Time, budget and safety limits affect what is feasible
questions.explanation: Constraints shape realistic options.

questions.question: When an unexpected result appears, what is a responsible response?
options: Change the data to match your theory
Check measurements and investigate possible causes
questions.explanation: Unexpected evidence deserves careful analysis.

questions.question: Which approach helps a team make a balanced decision?
options: Compare benefits, risks and evidence before choosing
Ask only one person to decide secretly
questions.explanation: Balanced decisions consider multiple relevant factors.
